messages:
emily: Heads-up: enterprise/private customers asked for clearer guidance on v1->v2 migration for on-prem/Dedicated. We need a short runbook + FAQ for SREs and a template email for account teams. Who can own?

alberto: I can draft the on-prem runbook. Key items: config changes, model alias injections, cert rotation notes, and a checklist for air-gapped installs.

molly: I'll take the FAQ + account email template. Need the exact deprecation dates and recommended migration window to set expectations.

raj: Deprecation date is 2026-06-01 for public hosted v1 endpoints. For Dedicated/Private we can offer extended timelines if customers opt into a compatibility shim, but we should encourage migration. We'll document SLA implications.

michael: For the runbook, include a verification step with small evals (a couple prompts and expected token deltas). I can produce the Python test harness snippets.

alberto: Sketch for runbook sections: 1) Pre-checklist (backup config, inventory models), 2) Apply model aliases mapping, 3) Update clients (snippets for curl / ts / py), 4) Restart services and run smoke evals, 5) Rollback steps, 6) Contact support links.

emily: Good. Please add a short troubleshooting subsection for quantization/precision regressions and GPU kernel mismatches.

docs-bot: Use label `enterprise-deprecation` and add tag `private-dedicated-guidance`. See template at docs/private-migration-template.md.

molly: Draft email snippet for accounts: 
"We are deprecating legacy v1 model endpoints. For hosted customers, removal is scheduled for 2026-06-01. If you run Dedicated or Private, we will coordinate an extended migration window and offer a compatibility wrapper. Please contact your account manager to schedule a migration briefing."

raj: Add a short bullet about billing changes: v2 uses per-token pricing slightly different; include example cost impact for a 100k monthly token workload.

alberto: For the compatibility shim, propose code both in TS and Go. Go is important for on-prem infra teams. I can add a minimal shim that rewrites request payloads and maps responses.

michael: Example quickcheck (py): 
```py
# small smoke eval to compare responses
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=...)
old = client.v1.generate(text='Hello')
new = client.v2.responses.create(input='Hello')
# assert similar length / basic contains
```
I'll expand and add tolerances.

emily: Also prepare a short support runbook for oncall: what to look for (increased latency, token mismatch, E2E test failures), and escalation matrix.

alberto: Will include sample commands for verifying model alias tables in DB and the kube rollout commands for Dedicated clusters.

molly: I'll coordinate with legal on required contract language for extended timelines.

ci-bot: Reminder: include links to the docs PRs in the migration checklist so CI can track examples.

emily: Let's split tasks: alberto = on-prem runbook + shim examples (TS/Go), michael = python smoke tests + CI examples, molly = FAQ + account email + legal check, raj = billing impact and support Qs, sara = add deprecation banner copy and update docs index. I'll create the tracker PR and assign reviewers.

alberto: One more thing: include a snippet for customers using KMS/HSM key rotation; they often trip on auth issues during migration.

molly: Noted. I'll add a checkbox to the account template to verify key access beforehand.

emily: Thanks all. Please open PRs in docs repo and link them here. We'll aim to ship the runbook + FAQ before the public banner goes live.

raj: I'll draft the support Q&A and link to this thread in the PR description.

emily: Closing loop: target to have drafts by Fri. Ping me in-thread when PRs are open. :rocket:
